title: Closed Sicilian & Grand Prix
intro: Answer 2.Nc3 with 2...Nc6 and a kingside fianchetto (...g6, ...Bg7). Against 2.f4, strike in the centre immediately with 2...d5.
variation: e2e4 c7c5 b1c3, e2e4 c7c5 f2f4

steps.text: In the Closed Sicilian, White develops 2.Nc3 instead of opening the centre with d4.

steps.hint: Develop your queen's knight to c6.
steps.ifWrong: Play 2...Nc6 to control d4 and e5.
steps.ifRight: Both knights now control the key d4 square.

steps.text: White prepares a kingside fianchetto with 3.g3.
Match White's fianchetto to fight for the dark squares.
steps.ifWrong: Play 3...g6 to put your bishop on g7.
steps.ifRight: From g7 the bishop aims straight through d4.

steps.text: White puts the bishop on g2: 4.Bg2.
Place your bishop on the long diagonal.
steps.hint: Move the f8 bishop to g7.

steps.text: White plays 5.d3, preparing Be3 and f4. Keep the g7 diagonal open.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5...d6 so your c8 bishop is free and you can follow with ...e6 and ...Nge7.
steps.ifRight: Next ...e6 and ...Nge7 keep f5 under control while preparing ...Rb8 and ...b5.

lessons.title: Meeting the Grand Prix (3.f4)
lessons.summary: Fianchetto with ...g6 and ...Bg7, and jump to d4 against Bb5.

steps.text: In the Grand Prix Attack, White pushes 3.f4 to aim for a direct attack on your kingside.
Use the same solid fianchetto set-up to blunt White's attack.
steps.ifWrong: Play 3...g6 to put your bishop on g7.
steps.ifRight: Your g7 bishop keeps e5 and d4 under pressure.
Now Black is ready for ...e6 and ...Nge7 (or ...Nd4 against Bb5).

steps.text: White plays 5.Bb5, threatening to double your c-pawns. Jump into the centre.
steps.hint: Hop to d4 with your c6 knight.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5...Nd4: it avoids doubled pawns and challenges White's strong f3 knight.
steps.ifRight: If White plays Nxd4, ...cxd4 gives Black great central control and queenside play.

steps.text: If White aims at f7 with 5.Bc4, shut down the diagonal at once.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5...e6 so White's c4 bishop hits a solid pawn wall and ...Nge7 is ready.
steps.ifRight: Next ...Nge7, ...O-O and ...d5 strike back in the centre.

lessons.title: Meeting an early 2.f4
lessons.summary: Counter in the centre at once with 2...d5 and 3...Nf6.

steps.text: If White plays 2.f4 immediately before Nc3, the d5 square is wide open.
Strike in the centre at once.
steps.ifWrong: Play 2...d5 to challenge e4 before White can defend it with Nc3.
steps.ifRight: White is forced to deal with the central tension immediately.

steps.text: Develop with an attack on d5 instead of bringing the queen out early.
steps.hint: Develop your king's knight to f6.
steps.ifWrong: Play 3...Nf6 so you recapture on d5 with the knight and lead in development.
steps.ifRight: Black wins d5 back effortlessly with a great position.

feedback.d8d5: 3...Qxd5 allows 4.Nc3, gaining time against your queen. Play 3...Nf6.

steps.text: White develops 4.Nc3. Recapture the central pawn cleanly.
steps.hint: Take on d5 with your knight.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4...Nxd5: after 5.Nxd5 Qxd5, your queen sits nicely in the centre because Nc3 is gone.
steps.ifRight: Black equalizes easily and targets White's weakened kingside.

steps.text: What if White checks with 4.Bb5+ to try to hold the d5 pawn?
steps.hint: Block the check with your c8 bishop.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4...Bd7 to challenge the bishop and win back d5 smoothly.
steps.ifRight: After 5.Bxd7+ Qxd7, Black recaptures on d5 next and stands very well.
